correctness.rationale: The polynomial coordinate shear is an exact time-preserving conjugacy to an axial skew product over the scalar Hamiltonian U; direct symbolic original-coordinate differentiation proves J³=0 and r>0 excludes equilibria. Four alternating simple stationary points produce two regular annuli with opposite-sign energy ranges. Center and nondegenerate saddle time-average limits of g(v) have opposite signs in each annulus; continuity, logarithmic saddle residence and the intermediate-value theorem guarantee two distinct zero-drift energies. Every lifted trajectory on either zero-drift oval closes after its minimal planar period. The equality K=3r/2 is included and handled. Independent verification script confirmed symbolic identities and six representative numerical drift roots.

originality.rationale: The original nilpotent polynomial field construction, polynomial conjugacy, and mere existence of two planar annuli are credited to Castañeda–Rebollo-Perdomo 2022. Their sole periodic-cylinder theorem is in a different linear-P1 subfamily; their Section 5 expressly asks about higher-degree periodic-surface multiplicity. Simultaneous vanishing of axial drift on the two wells, and hence two three-dimensional periodic cylinders in the quadratic-P1 family, is an additional statement not implied by the cited source. A close published even-kinetic skew-flow result has one annulus and non-nilpotent Jacobian. Residual risk of unindexed broader and inaccessible journal-version work remains.

value.rationale: The cited primary source explicitly poses the number of actual periodic surfaces as an open structural question when deg P1>1. Producing two distinct isochronous periodic cylinders within the same everywhere-nilpotent three-dimensional polynomial flow, with no equilibria and in a nontrivial full parameter region, directly addresses the question. The sign-change mechanism for separate original-time drift integrals is the meaningful mathematical content, not a routine relabeling of the original two-annulus example. The result does not claim a global maximum or classification beyond at least two.
